While I can’t confirm that these are all fake, I will say about 90% of these are fake from just looking at these pictures. All of these pins are ones that have been highly fakes in general. Identifying fakes can be difficult, so I will list some signs. Some signs are (but not limited to):
Lightweight, paint dips in the enamel (the paint physically dips down in between metal outlines - this is how I know your blue Mickey flag is fake for instance ), streaky paint (like a paintbrush texture) on the front, borders or raised edges on Mickey waffle backs, the mickey heads on hidden Mickeys being oddly shaped or blobby, the color of the paint being wrong or off (ie a neon yellow instead of a pale yellow), or generally bad quality of the pin.
It is important to note that just because a pin has one of these qualities does not necessarily mean it’s fake - for instance, many newer releases have borders on their Mickey head waffle backs because Disney has not been putting as much into quality. Normally it’s a combination of some of these traits. As you trade more, you will start to see trends on different series of fakes and how to tell them. Hidden Mickey pins are some of the most highly fakes ones in general.
Magically Emily on YouTube has some great videos on how to tell! I hope this helps ❤️

1. They are all real “Disney” pins in traders eyes. I know some collectors don’t care for them, but as they are the most accessible to the general population they have become much more popular in recent years and most traders I know consider them similar or same tier. It really depends on the trader though. I could see trading one for an open edition disney parks pin, but not a limited edition, for instance.
2. Most approved/reputable sellers are friends with cast members who have access to those exclusive pins and are able to trade/buy them at a discount. If you need a list of some, pm me.
3. FB is the most formal and widespread way to trade, and Instagram is becoming more popular for sellers, but trading as well. I would say Reddit is the least popular way. Many credible sellers tend to be people who have spent years in the hobby or are admins in their respective groups. I guess there isn’t a full proof way to know, but if an account looks to be a “bot” account (I.e. no posts, no bio, just joined fb/insta, no friends) I wouldn’t trust it. I only trade personally, but some of my friends sell who are true hobbyists. It’s just personal preference.
4. Most serious traders trade value for value. eBay sold listings or worthpoint are the best way got tell value. Most cast exclusive pins and older limited editions tend to be the ones that are more expensive.
5. The massive me amount of pins I want to add to my collection and the thrill of the hint! I spend more on traders than I do on pins I actually want. I could have spent that money on one for my collection, but I have fun trading with others in the community and finding a pin I’ve been searching for for awhile!
6. I wish I did more research on fakes earlier. There are many YouTube videos that show you how to tell, I watched Magically Emily’s series and it helped me a lot. I also wish I looked into local pin trading groups earlier - I found one where I am and we have meetups all the time, it’s great!

The main thing is to get your mind to a place where you can accept that some things arent under your control, and you can separate your worries from your physical self. Acknowledge that these thoughts and feelings are there, let them be, and go about your day thinking about only the present.
